idiom_name: protocol port + struct implementation with let collaborators (any Protocol)
implementation_notes: Value semantics do most of the work: make the service a struct whose collaborators are let properties, declare the domain port as a protocol in the domain module and inject the conformance through init - or as any Port when the implementation is chosen at run time. A struct cannot be mutated through a shared reference, so the 'no state' rule becomes a property of the type rather than a comment; when the operation has no collaborators at all, an enum with static functions is the idiomatic namespace and the role structure disappears.
pitfalls: A class with var properties or a lazy cache becomes shared mutable state the moment two callers hold the same instance; prefer structs or final classes with immutable storage.
Protocols with associated types or Self requirements cannot be used as existentials (any Port), forcing type erasure or generics - plan the port's shape accordingly.
Swift 6 concurrency checks Sendable: a service crossing actors must be Sendable, which reference types with mutable state are not.

variants.name: Service as a value of pure closures (point-free style)
variants.idiom_name: struct of function properties with live/test static members
variants.implementation_notes: Replace the protocol with a struct whose properties are closures (struct ExchangeRates { let rate: (Currency, Currency) -> Decimal }), build live and test values as static members, and make the domain operation a function taking that value. Every closure is independently injectable, so a caller depends on exactly the one operation it uses without declaring a new type, and decoration is just a function that returns a new value; choose the protocol form when conformances must be shared, when reference semantics are wanted, or when the surface is large enough that a missing implementation should be a compile error.
pitfalls: Nothing verifies that a hand-built value implements the whole contract: a missing or fatalError-backed closure fails at run time, so tests must exercise every operation the feature uses.
Closure properties must be @Sendable before the value can cross concurrency boundaries, and capturing non-Sendable objects defeats the purpose.
Value equality is meaningless for closure properties, so these structs cannot be compared or used as dictionary keys; that is a design signal, not a bug to fix.
